findings.title: Spurious-win return (and other errors) skip CQ teardown, leaving stack ops in the loop.
findings.detail: The file header and the generation-success path tear down with close(); cancelAll(.keep); drain, which is the documented single-driver contract. The path this reproducer exists to take does not: on error.Closed it prints SPURIOUS and `return error.Spurious`, and every `try` in `driver` (select, submit, yield) does the same. recv_op, t1, and cq live on the coroutine stack; cancel never runs, then the defers close the socketpair under an in-flight NetRecv. join() then returns that stack to the pool while the other seven workers keep running. ownerCallback will lock a freed CompletionQueue and push a freed group node; io_uring/kqueue may complete the recv on a recycled fd. The CQ tests themselves use `defer cq.cancelAll(.discard)` for exactly this. Put that defer next to `init()` (ops are frame-local, so .discard is the right Results), and only then return.

findings.title: POSIX-only sockets are registered for every target, so Windows cannot build examples.
findings.detail: build.zig adds cq-spurious-select-repro to the unconditional examples list (`zig build examples`, including check.sh --full). The program uses std.c.socketpair, std.c.fcntl, std.c.O.NONBLOCK, std.c.write/close, std.c.fd_t, and std.c.iovec. None of those are the Windows surface: socketpair is OperationUnsupported there, fcntl/O_* do not exist, NetHandle is SOCKET, and ReadBuf.fromSlice takes os.iovec (WSABUF, not std.c.iovec). The rest of the examples go through zio.os.net, which already has socketpair (POSIX, including Darwin nonblock-via-fcntl) and createLoopbackSocketPair (Windows). Use those, write through zio.os.net as well, and keep feed_fd as ev.Backend.NetHandle / os.net.fd_t with the platform invalid value — or omit the example on Windows. As landed, `zig build examples -Dtarget=x86_64-windows` and a native Windows examples build fail.
